SickLeaveCase.title: Sick leave case
SickLeaveCase.description: An administrative sickness case (ziekmelding) tracking the Wet verbetering poortwachter (WVP) re-integration process and statutory loondoorbetaling — NEVER medical data. Per the AVG and the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens beleidsregels "De zieke werknemer", an employer may record that and how long an employee is sick and the re-integration process facts, but never the nature or cause of the illness: this schema declares no diagnosis, symptom, cause, or medical-note field of any kind (leave-verzuim-mvp REQ-VWP-002). The gemeld<->hersteld lifecycle is fully declarative per ADR-031; a relapse within 4 weeks of recovery reopens the same case rather than starting a new one (samengesteld ziektegeval, BW 7:629 lid 10). The four WVP milestone Due dates (probleemanalyse week 6, plan van aanpak week 8, UWV 42-wekenmelding week 42, eerstejaarsevaluatie week 52) are derived from firstSickDay but stored, not computed on the fly — the loonaangifte-filing-lifecycle deadline precedent — so the dossier shows the clock actually worked against and a UWV-granted deferral stays editable; derivation correctness is enforced by the nl-wvp-milestone-derivation rule check (lib/Standards/rules/labour.json), not recomputed away.

herstellen.description: The employee has recovered. recoveredDate is stamped on the carrying write (the Timesheet approvedAt/approvedBy pattern).

heropenen.description: Relapse within 4 weeks of recovery continues the same case as one samengesteld ziektegeval (BW 7:629 lid 10) rather than starting a new 104-week clock. recoveredDate is cleared on the carrying write.

employeeId.title: Employee
employeeId.x-notes: UUID reference to the sick employee.

firstSickDay.title: First sick day
firstSickDay.description: The first day of this sickness period (dag 1 ziek) — the anchor date every WVP milestone Due date is derived from (+6/8/42/52 weeks).

recoveredDate.title: Recovered date
recoveredDate.description: When the employee recovered. Cleared again if the case is reopened.
recoveredDate.x-notes: Date the employee recovered, stamped on the herstellen carrying write and cleared on the heropenen carrying write.

status.title: Status
status.description: Whether this case is open (reported) or closed (recovered).
status.x-notes: Case lifecycle status. Governed by the x-openregister-lifecycle state machine (gemeld <-> hersteld).

wachtdag.title: Waiting day
wachtdag.description: Whether the first sick day is treated as an unpaid waiting day, where the CAO/contract provides for one.

loondoorbetalingPercentage.title: Continued-pay percentage
loondoorbetalingPercentage.description: How much of the wage continues during sickness. The legal minimum is 70% for the first 104 weeks, with a minimum-wage floor in the first year.
loondoorbetalingPercentage.x-notes: Percentage of wages continued during sickness. Statutory minimum is 70% for the first 104 weeks (BW art. 7:629 lid 1), with a first-year floor at the statutory minimum wage. Checked on open cases by nl-loondoorbetaling-minimum.

aangepastLoon.title: Adjusted wage
aangepastLoon.description: Wages still earned from partial work in this period. Leave empty when the employee is fully absent.
aangepastLoon.x-notes: The wage still earned from partial work during this sickness period (samengesteld/aangepast loon) — composed with the continuation on the remainder by the sick-pay calculator (BW art. 7:629 lid 1). Null/absent means fully sick (treated as 0).

probleemanalyseDue.title: Problem analysis due
probleemanalyseDue.description: Deadline for the problem analysis: six weeks after the first day of sickness.
probleemanalyseDue.x-notes: Statutory deadline for the probleemanalyse: firstSickDay + 6 weeks (Regeling procesgang eerste en tweede ziektejaar art. 2). Derived but stored (audit trail + UWV-deferral editability); checked by nl-wvp-milestone-derivation / nl-wvp-milestone-overdue.

probleemanalyseDone.title: Problem analysis done
probleemanalyseDone.description: Date the probleemanalyse was actually completed.

planVanAanpakDue.title: Action plan due
planVanAanpakDue.description: Deadline for the action plan: eight weeks after the first day of sickness.
planVanAanpakDue.x-notes: Statutory deadline for the plan van aanpak: firstSickDay + 8 weeks (Regeling procesgang art. 2).

planVanAanpakDone.title: Action plan done
planVanAanpakDone.description: Date the action plan was actually completed.
planVanAanpakDone.x-notes: Date the plan van aanpak was actually completed.

uwv42WeekMeldingDue.title: UWV 42-week notification due
uwv42WeekMeldingDue.description: Deadline for the 42-week notification to the UWV: 42 weeks after the first day of sickness.
uwv42WeekMeldingDue.x-notes: Statutory deadline for the UWV 42-wekenmelding: firstSickDay + 42 weeks (ZW art. 38).

uwv42WeekMeldingDone.title: UWV 42-week notification done
uwv42WeekMeldingDone.description: When the 42-week notification was filed with the UWV. Recorded here only — this app does not send it.
uwv42WeekMeldingDone.x-notes: Date the 42-wekenmelding was actually filed with UWV. Recorded here only — this app does not transmit it (no UWV wire integration).

eerstejaarsevaluatieDue.title: First-year evaluation due
eerstejaarsevaluatieDue.description: Deadline for the first-year evaluation: 52 weeks after the first day of sickness.
eerstejaarsevaluatieDue.x-notes: Statutory deadline for the eerstejaarsevaluatie: firstSickDay + 52 weeks (Regeling procesgang art. 4).

eerstejaarsevaluatieDone.title: First-year evaluation done
eerstejaarsevaluatieDone.description: Date the eerstejaarsevaluatie was actually completed.

absenceProgression.title: Absence progression
absenceProgression.description: How the return to work progresses: each step sets the percentage the employee is absent from a given date onwards.
absenceProgression.x-notes: The time-resolved record of partial work resumption (gedeeltelijke werkhervatting) during this case: an ordered series of steps, each setting the percentage of contracted hours the employee is absent from `effectiveFrom` onward until the next step. This is the field a verzuimpercentage is computed from -- without it an absence can only be counted as whole calendar days, which overstates every case where the employee is partly back at work. ADMINISTRATIVE ONLY, and lawful for exactly that reason: the AP beleidsregels "De zieke werknemer" permit an employer to record TO WHAT EXTENT an employee can resume work (it drives loondoorbetaling and the WVP re-integration duty) while forbidding why -- so this array carries a date and a percentage and nothing else, and REQ-VWP-002's ban on diagnosis, symptom, cause and unconstrained free text holds unchanged. EMPTY OR ABSENT MEANS FULL ABSENCE for the whole case window: every case recorded before this field existed keeps counting exactly as it did, so adding the field regresses no figure. The euro-denominated `aangepastLoon` is the sibling of this field, not a duplicate of it -- that one carries what was still earned, this one carries when and how much was worked.

effectiveFrom.title: Effective from
effectiveFrom.description: First day this absence percentage applies. A date before the first sick day counts from the first sick day; a date after the case closed has no effect.
effectiveFrom.x-notes: First day on which this absence percentage applies. A step dated before firstSickDay is clipped to firstSickDay; a step dated after the case closed contributes nothing.

absencePercentage.title: Absence percentage
absencePercentage.description: How much of the contracted hours the employee is absent from that date on. 100 means not working at all, 40 means working 60% of the hours. Entering 0 records a full return to work, but it does not close the case — the recovery date does that.
absencePercentage.x-notes: Percentage of contracted hours the employee is absent from effectiveFrom onward. 100 = not working at all, 40 = working 60% of contracted hours. 0 records a full resumption, but it is NOT what closes the case: recoveredDate and the gemeld/hersteld lifecycle stay the single authority on that, and the calculation clips at recoveredDate regardless of what this array says.

currentAbsencePercentage.title: Current absence percentage
currentAbsencePercentage.description: The absence percentage from the most recent step that has taken effect.
currentAbsencePercentage.x-notes: The absencePercentage of the latest absenceProgression step that has taken effect -- a stored projection, so an index column and a filter can read it without walking the array (the Jaaropgaaf aggregate precedent). NEVER read by AbsenceRateService: every rate is computed from absenceProgression itself, so a stale projection cannot corrupt a reported figure. Null on a case with no progression steps, which per that field's contract means fully absent, not unknown.

administrationId.title: Administration
administrationId.description: Which administration this case belongs to. Normally the same as the employee's.
administrationId.x-notes: Denormalized administratie key this SickLeaveCase is scoped to (multi-administratie, REQ-MULTI-001). Optional, nullable plain string -- NOT a $ref (ADR-062 rule 7), mirroring its employee's administrationId; maintained by HR/back-office and audited for drift by nl-administratie-scope-consistency (REQ-MULTI-007). The implicit page scoping (REQ-MULTI-004) filters on it.

Stagiair.title: Intern
Stagiair.description: A person on a stageovereenkomst (HBO/WO/MBO-BOL, zonder dienstverband), tracked by humaniq but explicitly NOT an Employee, NOT payroll-engine input, and NOT CAO-scoped (stagiair-bbl-admin design.md D1). A stagiair has no arbeidsovereenkomst and, in the ordinary case, no loonheffing on the stagevergoeding, so it is modelled structurally separate from Employee/EmploymentContract: no payroll schema (PayrollRun, Payslip, PayrollMutationReport) references Stagiair and PayrollCalculator never reads it, so a stagiair can never reach the loon path by accident. A BBL-leerling is NOT a Stagiair -- it has a real leerarbeidsovereenkomst and is an EmploymentContract with type: bbl (design.md D1). Governed by a plain three-transition declarative x-openregister-lifecycle (aangemeld -> lopend -> afgerond/gestopt), no guard needed.

starten.description: The stage placement has started; startDate has been reached and the stagiair is actively on placement.

afronden.description: The stage placement completed successfully; the case is closed out.

stoppen.description: The stage placement was terminated early (by the stagiair, the onderwijsinstelling, or the leerbedrijf) before it reached afgerond.

onderwijsinstelling.title: Educational institution
onderwijsinstelling.description: Name of the educational institution (hogeschool/universiteit/ROC) the stagiair is enrolled at and that placed them on this stage.

opleiding.title: Study programme
opleiding.description: The programme (opleiding) the stagiair is following at the onderwijsinstelling, e.g. 'HBO Bedrijfskunde' or 'WO Rechtsgeleerdheid'.

niveau.title: Education level
niveau.description: The intern's education level. All three are placements without an employment contract; an apprentice on a work-study contract is an employee instead.
niveau.x-notes: Education level of the stagiair. 'hbo' (hoger beroepsonderwijs) / 'wo' (wetenschappelijk onderwijs) / 'mbo-bol' (middelbaar beroepsonderwijs, beroepsopleidende leerweg). All three are stageovereenkomst-based (zonder dienstverband); a BBL (beroepsbegeleidende leerweg) leerling is NOT modelled here -- it has a leerarbeidsovereenkomst and is an EmploymentContract with type: bbl (design.md D1).

stagetype.title: Placement type
stagetype.description: The kind of placement. For information only — it has no effect on pay or compliance.
stagetype.x-notes: Kind of stage. 'snuffelstage' (orientation), 'meeloopstage' (work-shadowing), or 'afstudeerstage' (graduation placement). Informational; carries no payroll or compliance meaning.

startDate.title: Start date
startDate.description: First day of the placement. Once it has passed, a signed placement agreement must be on file.
startDate.x-notes: First day of the stage placement (ISO 8601). Anchor date for nl-bpv-overeenkomst-vereist: once startDate has passed, a signed BPV-overeenkomst (bpvOvereenkomstOndertekend true) must be on file.

endDate.title: End date
endDate.description: Planned last day of the placement. Leave empty when it is open-ended.
endDate.x-notes: Planned last day of the stage placement (ISO 8601), or null when open-ended.

begeleiderId.title: Supervisor
begeleiderId.description: The colleague supervising this intern. Leave empty until one is assigned.
begeleiderId.x-notes: UUID reference to the Employee acting as the internal stagebegeleider (supervisor) for this stagiair. Nullable when no supervisor is assigned yet. This is the ONLY relation on Stagiair; it points from Stagiair to Employee, never the reverse, and no payroll schema ever references Stagiair (design.md D1).

stagevergoedingPerMaand.title: Placement allowance per month
stagevergoedingPerMaand.description: Any monthly allowance paid to the intern. Recorded for information; it is not put through payroll here.
stagevergoedingPerMaand.x-notes: Optional monthly stagevergoeding paid to the stagiair, stored as a plain informational figure only. The fiscal treatment of a stagevergoeding is governed by the Belastingdienst Handboek Loonheffingen (hoofdstuk 17, 'Stagiairs', https://www.belastingdienst.nl/wps/wcm/connect/bldcontentnl/belastingdienst/zakelijk/personeel_en_loon/personeel_in_dienst/stagiairs): a stagiair zonder dienstbetrekking is, in the ordinary case the handbook describes, not automatically loonheffingplichtig the way an employee's loon is, but the actual test turns on concrete facts (who pays, whether it is capped to daadwerkelijke onkosten, the studenten- en scholierenregeling). No specific untaxed euro ceiling is asserted by humaniq and NO machine-checkable rule enforces one, because no confirmed threshold is cited (design.md D2); a future rule would need the exact Belastingdienst figure with a {value, source, verified} leaf (verified:false + checkAgainst URL) before asserting a limit.

bpvOvereenkomstOndertekend.title: Placement agreement signed
bpvOvereenkomstOndertekend.description: The three-party placement agreement has been signed. Tick this by hand once signing is done.
bpvOvereenkomstOndertekend.x-notes: Whether the (three-party) stage-/BPV-overeenkomst is signed, marked manually by HR after the paper or externally-handled signing is complete -- mirroring EmploymentContract.writtenContract exactly. NOT an automated e-signature flow: two of the three signers (onderwijsinstelling contactpersoon, deelnemer) are not ordinarily Nextcloud users of this instance, and the shipped docudesk signing leaf cannot complete for a non-NC-user signer (offer-esign design.md point 4, design.md D3). Gates nl-bpv-overeenkomst-vereist: must be true once startDate has passed.

verzekeringGeverifieerd.title: Insurance verified
verzekeringGeverifieerd.description: HR has checked that the intern's liability and accident cover is in place.
verzekeringGeverifieerd.x-notes: Whether the stagiair's insurance cover (aansprakelijkheid/ongevallen) has been verified by HR. Informational HR-entered attestation; carries no machine-checkable rule in this change.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where this placement has got to: registered, ongoing, completed, or terminated early.
status.x-notes: Placement lifecycle status. Governed by the x-openregister-lifecycle state machine (aangemeld -> lopend -> afgerond, with gestopt as an early-termination terminal from aangemeld/lopend). Defaults to aangemeld.

administrationId.title: Administration
administrationId.description: Which administration this placement belongs to.
administrationId.x-notes: Denormalized administratie key this Stagiair is scoped to (multi-administratie, REQ-MULTI-001). Optional, nullable plain string -- NOT a $ref (ADR-062 rule 7, the PayrollRun convention); maintained by HR/back-office when the record is created and used for the implicit page scoping (REQ-MULTI-004).

TimeEntry.x-notes: hours-process-redesign: this cost-allocation extension moved from Timesheet to TimeEntry — allocation describes what a specific booking was worked on, which is per-entry, not per-period. The former Timesheet-level copies were dropped rather than kept as denormalized aggregates: no PHP, manifest or event-contract consumer reads them (PayrollGLPostService and the approved-time-entry CloudEvent were checked), so a retained copy would be a dead declaration. None of these three properties ever appears on a form: they are written by integrations, not people.

domainObjectRef.title: Domain object reference
domainObjectRef.description: The external case or dossier this booking was worked on, when hours are logged from another application.
domainObjectRef.x-notes: Optional UUID of the external domain object — a procest case, a decidesk dossier, anything outside humaniq (ADR-081 decision 5). Plain string, not a $ref relation, because the target schema does not exist in humaniq (ADR-062 rule 7 — the same reasoning as projectId and clientRef). Distinct from projectId: a case is not a project, and conflating them would make the resulting cost allocation ambiguous about what it is costing.

domainObjectType.title: Domain object type
domainObjectType.description: Which app and record type the reference points at.
domainObjectType.x-notes: Format `<app>:<schema>` — e.g. `procest:case` (ADR-081 decision 5). Without it a bare UUID is unresolvable: humaniq cannot ask 'which app owns this?' and neither can the receiving bookkeeping app. Set together with domainObjectRef or not at all.

allocationKey.title: Ledger allocation key
allocationKey.description: The bookkeeping category these hours are charged to, filled in by the connected bookkeeping system.
allocationKey.x-notes: The ledger dimension the resulting cost is booked against, OPAQUE to humaniq (ADR-081 decision 5). For a Dutch municipality this is the BBV taakveld code the domain app resolved from its own classification (procest: caseType.iv3Taakveld); another jurisdiction books against something else entirely. humaniq deliberately does not model, validate or translate it — Shillinq owns the taakveld catalogue, and a BBV-shaped field in an HR app would couple humaniq to one country's accounting law. Stamped by the app that logs the hours, at the moment it logs them, so the allocation reflects the classification in force then rather than a later reclassification. Never hand-typed by an employee (product decision 5/6); outside every includeFields allowlist.

employeeId.title: Employee
employeeId.description: The employee these hours were worked by.
employeeId.x-notes: Self-service surfaces never show this field: TimeEntryStampListener resolves it from the signed-in user's own Employee record (nextcloudUserId match) and REFUSES the write when no employee is linked — the listener is the enforcement point, which is why the property is deliberately NOT in the schema's required list: OpenRegister validates required-ness BEFORE the pre-save creating event, so a schema-required employeeId would reject every self-service booking before the listener could resolve it. The HR entry page (TimeEntries) offers it as a picker. format:uuid is correct and deliberate: OpenRegister's own ValidateObject rewrites a $ref relation to a uuid-patterned string, so a uuid IS the canonical stored form of a relation. Seed data addresses the target by slug through the `@ref:<slug>` token, which ImportHandler resolves to the real uuid BEFORE validation runs — so the format rejects nothing legitimate. It was briefly dropped here on the theory that slugs were a valid stored form; that was the wrong call, because the format is the only thing that makes a broken reference fail LOUDLY instead of persisting as referential garbage no surface can resolve.

timesheetId.title: Timesheet
timesheetId.description: The period timesheet this booking is part of. Assigned automatically from the start date.
timesheetId.x-notes: Never a form field. TimeEntryStampListener resolves the employee's draft/rejected Timesheet for the month of startedAt (YYYY-MM grain, fixed by design resolution 2) and creates a draft Timesheet when none exists. Booking into a period whose only timesheet is submitted/approved is refused — never silently forked into a second timesheet. Always a real uuid: the listener and MigrateHoursProcess both assign the parent timesheet's own id, and seed data uses the `@ref:<slug>` token that ImportHandler resolves before validation — see employeeId's note for why format:uuid stays.

breakMinutes.title: Break (minutes)
breakMinutes.description: Unpaid break time to subtract from this booking.

hours.title: Hours
hours.description: Worked hours in this booking, calculated from start, end and break.
hours.x-notes: Server-derived on every write by TimeEntryStampListener: (endedAt - startedAt - breakMinutes)/60, rounded to 2 decimals. A booking whose end does not lie after its start, or whose break exceeds the span, is refused with a structured 422 (REQ-TEC-001). Not readOnly: the deriving listener itself must write it, and OpenRegister enforces readOnly on every UPDATE with no backend bypass.

projectId.title: Project
projectId.description: The project these hours were worked on.
projectId.x-notes: Plain string, not a $ref relation: no Project schema is modeled in humaniq (ADR-062 rule 7 — only fields whose target exists in this register set get $ref). The one allocation-adjacent field an employee may choose on the booking form.

billable.title: Billable
billable.description: Whether these hours are billable to a client or project.

costCenter.title: Cost centre
costCenter.description: The cost centre these hours count against, derived from the employee's team.
costCenter.x-notes: Never a form field (product decision 6). Stamped by TimeEntryStampListener via OrgResolutionService: the employee's active OrgAssignment unit's OrgUnit.costCenter. Null when the chain does not resolve — never guessed.

userId.title: User
userId.description: The account these hours belong to.
userId.x-notes: Denormalized Nextcloud user id (mijn-hr-self-service) — a plain NC-user-id string mirroring the approvedBy convention, never a $ref. A copy of the linked Employee's nextcloudUserId, carried because the manifest filter grammar cannot join across schemas; the MijnUren page filters on it with the @me token. Re-stamped from employeeId on every write by TimeEntryStampListener, so it cannot drift.

administrationId.title: Administration
administrationId.description: The administration these hours belong to.
administrationId.x-notes: Denormalized administratie key (multi-administratie, REQ-MULTI-001) — plain string, NOT a $ref (ADR-062 rule 7). Stamped from the resolved Employee's administrationId by TimeEntryStampListener; for hours booking the administration is always derivable from the employment, so no hours surface carries an administration form field.

origin.title: Origin
origin.x-notes: The one safe readOnly use in this schema pair (Decision 2 analysis): genuinely immutable after create, optional, defaulted, and stamped only on the CREATE write where OpenRegister's readOnly enforcement does not apply. 'migration' marks the synthetic entries the MigrateHoursProcess repair step fabricates for legacy timesheets — their timestamps are bookkeeping artifacts, not claims about when work happened.

TimeEntry.title: Time entry
TimeEntry.description: One individual booking of worked hours (urenregistratie): when the work started and ended, what it was, and optionally which project it was for. Bookings are collected automatically into the employee's monthly timesheet, which is what gets submitted for approval.

Timesheet.title: Timesheet
Timesheet.description: The monthly collection of an employee's hour bookings (urenstaat). Totals are kept up to date automatically while the employee books; once submitted, a manager approves or rejects the whole month.
Timesheet.x-notes: hours-process-redesign Decision 2: the period aggregate half of the former all-in-one schema — the approval lifecycle stays here and only here (a TimeEntry has none). The approval lifecycle is the correctly-homed HR/labour surface pipelinq's 'Timesheet approval' deep-link previously pointed at shillinq for; shillinq's UrenRegistratie is an append-only billing time-log with no approval state. hours/entryCount/projectId/costCenter/billable are server-recomputed aggregates (TimesheetAggregateListener, REQ-TEC-004) and the process fields are stamped on lifecycle edges (TimesheetProcessStampListener) — none of them is readOnly because humaniq's own listeners must write them and OpenRegister enforces readOnly on every UPDATE with no backend bypass; forms hide them via page-level includeFields allowlists instead. Two listeners write this schema (stamp + aggregate); both are recompute-style, so a stale intermediate total from concurrent entry writes is self-healed by the next write (accepted for dev-stage volumes).

submit.description: The employee submits the timesheet for manager approval. A rejected timesheet may be corrected and re-submitted. An empty timesheet (no bookings, or zero hours) cannot be submitted.

approve.description: A manager approves the submitted timesheet. The NoSelfApprovalGuard rejects self-approval (the approver may not be the claiming employee); approvedBy and approvedAt are stamped on the carrying write.

reject.description: A manager rejects the submitted timesheet (with a rejectionReason). The NoSelfApprovalGuard rejects self-rejection. The employee may correct it and re-submit.

reopen.description: Return an approved timesheet to draft for correction before it is consumed by payroll.

employeeId.title: Employee
employeeId.description: The employee whose hours this timesheet collects.
employeeId.x-notes: Drives the self-approval guard — the approver may not equal this employee. Required here (unlike TimeEntry.employeeId, which the stamp listener resolves after validation), and format:uuid: a uuid is the canonical stored form of a $ref relation in OpenRegister, and seed data reaches the target through the `@ref:<slug>` token that ImportHandler resolves before validation. Dropping the format would let a broken employee link persist silently — every surface that joins on it (userId/managerUserId stamping, the Mijn and team pages, nl-mss-manager-consistency) would then read as 'no link' rather than 'bad data'.

period.title: Period
period.description: The month this timesheet covers, as YYYY-MM.
period.x-notes: Month grain is fixed for auto-created timesheets (design resolution 2). Week grains (YYYY-Www / YYYY-Wnn-D) remain accepted for pre-existing data only.

hours.title: Hours
hours.description: Total hours worked this period, calculated automatically from the individual bookings.
hours.x-notes: Server-recomputed aggregate: sum of hours over the TimeEntry rows referencing this timesheet (REQ-TEC-004, TimesheetAggregateListener). Client input is inert. Reused by OpenRegister aggregations for per-employee and per-period totals.

entryCount.title: Bookings
entryCount.description: How many individual bookings this timesheet contains.
entryCount.x-notes: Server-recomputed aggregate (REQ-TEC-004). Lets TimesheetNotEmptyGuard and the UI distinguish 'no bookings' from 'bookings summing to 0 hours' — a guard is read-only over the payload it is handed, so it needs this maintained value.

description.title: Description
description.description: A note about this timesheet as a whole.
description.x-notes: The only field on the timesheet edit form (Decision 8: TimesheetDetail includeFields is exactly ['description']).

projectId.title: Project
projectId.description: The project all hours this period were worked on — filled in only when every booking names the same project.
projectId.x-notes: Denormalized aggregate for the approved-time-entry event contract (REQ-TEC-003): the single shared value when all entries agree, else null (emitted as ''). Plain string, not a $ref — no Project schema in humaniq (ADR-062 rule 7). Server-recomputed; client input inert.

costCenter.title: Cost centre
costCenter.description: The cost centre all hours this period count against — filled in only when every booking shares one.
costCenter.x-notes: Denormalized aggregate for the event contract, same homogeneous-or-null rule as projectId. Per-booking truth lives on TimeEntry.costCenter (derived from the org structure). Plain string, not a $ref — no CostCenter schema in humaniq.

billable.title: Billable
billable.description: Whether every booking this period is billable.
billable.x-notes: Denormalized aggregate for the event contract: true iff all entries are billable (REQ-TEC-003). Server-recomputed; client input inert.

clientRef.title: Client
clientRef.description: The client who reviews and approves the billable hours on this timesheet.
clientRef.x-notes: A domain-object reference, never a Nextcloud user id (ADR-046 A4). Cross-app reference: the target `client` schema lives in pipelinq's register, not humaniq's, so this is a plain identifier rather than an OpenRegister relation — see x-external-register. Deliberately NOT a $ref: OpenRegister resolves $ref within one register set, so a $ref here would name a schema it can never resolve. Scopes the read-only client view in the shared external portal (portaliq scopeField).

userId.title: User
userId.description: The account this timesheet belongs to. Kept up to date automatically.
userId.x-notes: Denormalized Nextcloud user id of the employee (mijn-hr-self-service) — a plain NC-user-id string mirroring the approvedBy convention, never a $ref. A copy of the linked Employee's nextcloudUserId, carried because the manifest filter grammar cannot join across schemas; MijnUrenstaten filters on it with the @me token. Server-stamped on every write by TimesheetProcessStampListener (custody change: no longer HR hand-entry); rows whose employee has no linked account keep null and never appear on a Mijn page (fail-closed, REQ-MHS-002).

managerUserId.title: Manager
managerUserId.description: The team manager who reviews this timesheet — kept up to date automatically from the organisation structure.
managerUserId.x-notes: Denormalized Nextcloud user id cache (mss-team-scope) — plain string, never a $ref. Assignment truth lives ONLY on the org structure (active OrgAssignment -> OrgUnit.managerId -> manager Employee's nextcloudUserId); this cache exists solely because the manifest filter grammar cannot join across schemas for the TeamUrengoedkeuring @me filter. Stamped by TimesheetProcessStampListener via the shared OrgResolutionService — the same code path the nl-mss-manager-consistency audit evaluates, so stamp and audit cannot disagree. Client input is inert.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where this timesheet is in the approval process.
status.x-notes: Lifecycle field, moved only by the x-openregister-lifecycle transitions. TimesheetProcessStampListener forces 'draft' on create and lets only transition-carried edges through on update.

submittedAt.title: Submitted at
submittedAt.description: When the timesheet was submitted for approval.
submittedAt.x-notes: Process field: stamped (ISO 8601 UTC) by TimesheetProcessStampListener on the submit edge, cleared on reopen; inert to client input on every other write.

approvedBy.title: Approved by
approvedBy.description: Who approved or rejected this timesheet.
approvedBy.x-notes: Nextcloud user ID of the acting manager — an NC user id, not an object FK, so it stays plain per ADR-046. Stamped from the acting session uid on the approve/reject edges; must differ from the claiming employee (NoSelfApprovalGuard). Inert to client input.

approvedAt.title: Approved at
approvedAt.description: When the timesheet was approved or rejected.
approvedAt.x-notes: Process field: ISO 8601 UTC, stamped on the approve/reject edges alongside approvedBy; inert to client input.

rejectionReason.title: Rejection reason
rejectionReason.description: Why the timesheet was rejected, shown to the employee so it can be corrected and re-submitted.
rejectionReason.x-notes: The single allowlisted client-supplied process value, accepted ONLY on the submitted->rejected edge (Decision 4). On every other write the stored value is restored. Interactive capture at reject time is gated on dependency items D1 (openregister transition inputs) and D2 (nc-vue prompt dialog); until they land the interim reject path leaves it empty, matching pre-redesign behaviour.

administrationId.title: Administration
administrationId.description: The administration this timesheet belongs to.
administrationId.x-notes: Denormalized administratie key (multi-administratie, REQ-MULTI-001) — plain string, NOT a $ref (ADR-062 rule 7, the PayrollRun/managerUserId convention), mirroring its employee's administrationId. Custody change: stamped by TimesheetProcessStampListener from the Employee (no longer HR hand-maintained); still audited for drift by nl-administratie-scope-consistency (REQ-MULTI-007). The implicit page scoping (REQ-MULTI-004) filters on it.

Vacancy.title: Vacancy
Vacancy.description: A job vacancy (vacature) published by the employer. Models the ADR-001 menu-6 'Onboarding & ATS' recruiting surface (recruiting-ats-basic): a declarative concept -> gepubliceerd -> gesloten publish lifecycle, no external multiposting (werk.nl/LinkedIn is an OpenConnector follow-up) and no public career page (portaliq per ADR-046). Applications reference this Vacancy via Application.vacancyId.

publiceren.description: The vacancy is published (inside humaniq only — no external channel wiring in the MVP). publishedDate is stamped on the carrying write (the Timesheet approvedAt/approvedBy pattern).

sluiten.description: The vacancy is closed. Terminal — no re-open and no publish-from-closed edge; a closed vacancy is re-created, not resurrected.

title.title: Title
title.description: The job title as it appears in the advert.

department.title: Department
department.description: Department or team the vacancy belongs to.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where this vacancy has got to: draft, published or closed.
status.x-notes: Publish workflow status. Governed by the x-openregister-lifecycle state machine (concept -> gepubliceerd -> gesloten).

publishedDate.title: Published date
publishedDate.x-notes: Date the vacancy was published, stamped on the publiceren carrying write.

closingDate.title: Closing date
closingDate.description: The application deadline. For information only — it does not close the vacancy by itself.
closingDate.x-notes: Application deadline. Informational only in the MVP — it does not drive the sluiten transition.

administrationId.title: Administration
administrationId.description: Which administration this vacancy belongs to.
administrationId.x-notes: Denormalized administratie key this Vacancy is scoped to (multi-administratie, REQ-MULTI-001). Optional, nullable plain string -- NOT a $ref (ADR-062 rule 7); a vacancy has no employee to derive it from, so nl-administratie-scope-consistency does not evaluate this schema.

WkrAssessment.title: WKR Assessment
WkrAssessment.description: The per-(administrationId, year) computed vrije-ruimte/eindheffing summary AND the reporting record (wkr-administration, the PayrollMutationReport precedent): produced ONLY by WkrService::assess(), rolling the cross-object fiscale loonsom (Σ Payslip.grossPay) and the administration's WkrDeclarations into the available vrije ruimte, the used amount, the excess and the 80% eindheffing exposure. Idempotently keyed on (administrationId, year): recomputing upserts this record in place, never duplicates. Persisting the assessment as a real object (rather than a transient calculation) is what makes nl-wkr-eindheffing-exposure RuleEngine-reachable -- the standing audit loads every WkrAssessment and checks it automatically.

administrationId.title: Administration ID
administrationId.description: Which administration this assessment covers.
administrationId.x-notes: The administration this assessment covers (wkr-administration REQ-WKR-003). Idempotent key together with year -- plain string, not a $ref (ADR-062 rule 7, the PayrollRun convention).

year.title: Year
year.description: The tax year this assessment covers.
year.x-notes: The fiscal year this assessment covers (wkr-administration REQ-WKR-003).

fiscaleLoonsom.title: Taxable wage bill
fiscaleLoonsom.description: Total gross pay across this administration and year, used to work out the free margin.
fiscaleLoonsom.x-notes: Σ Payslip.grossPay over this administration/year -- the fiscale-loonsom proxy WkrService reads (design.md Risks: an honest, auditable proxy for the exact kolom-14 loonsom, never a recomputed payroll figure).

vrijeRuimte.title: Free margin
vrijeRuimte.description: The free margin available, derived from the total wage bill.
vrijeRuimte.x-notes: Available vrije ruimte, computed from fiscaleLoonsom against the `wkr` group tranche percentages/grens in the active tax-year table (wkr-administration REQ-WKR-002).

vrijeRuimteUsed.title: Free margin used
vrijeRuimteUsed.description: Everything charged to the free margin this year: allowances on payslips plus separately declared ones.
vrijeRuimteUsed.x-notes: Σ Payslip.wkrUsed + Σ WkrDeclaration.amount where wkrCategory = 'vrije-ruimte', for this administration/year.

vrijeRuimteRemaining.title: Free margin remaining
vrijeRuimteRemaining.description: What is left of the free margin, never below zero.

excess.title: Excess
excess.description: How far the free margin was exceeded. Zero when it was not. This is the amount the 80% final levy applies to.
excess.x-notes: vrijeRuimteUsed minus vrijeRuimte when positive, else 0 -- the amount subject to the 80% eindheffing.

eindheffingRate.title: Final levy rate
eindheffingRate.description: The final levy rate applied to the excess — 80. Empty when there is no excess.
eindheffingRate.x-notes: The eindheffing rate (80, from the `wkr` table group) applied to the excess; null when excess is 0 (nl-wkr-eindheffing-exposure).

eindheffingDue.title: Final levy due
eindheffingDue.description: The final levy owed over the amount above the free margin.
eindheffingDue.x-notes: 80% of excess, rounded to the cent -- the eindheffing the employer owes over the vrije-ruimte overrun (settlement itself is a named fast-follow, not automated by this schema).

status.title: Status
status.description: Whether this administration stayed within its free margin, or owes a final levy on the excess.
status.x-notes: Whether the administration/year stayed within its vrije ruimte, or an eindheffing is owed over the excess (wkr-administration REQ-WKR-003/-WKR-004).

engineVersion.title: Engine version
engineVersion.description: The tables id (e.g. "nl-2026") this assessment's vrije-ruimte/eindheffing figures were computed against.

assessedAt.title: Assessed at
assessedAt.description: When this assessment was last calculated.
assessedAt.x-notes: When this assessment was (re)computed by WkrService::assess().

WkrDeclaration.title: WKR Declaration
WkrDeclaration.description: One recorded werkkostenregeling (WKR) vergoeding/verstrekking/terbeschikkingstelling for an administration (wkr-administration): a company-wide allowance/benefit (staff outing, Christmas hamper, fixed-cost allowance) or an employee-specific one, categorised so the administration-level vrije-ruimte roll-up (WkrService) knows whether it consumes the vrije ruimte, stays outside it as a gerichte vrijstelling, or was already designated eindheffingsloon.

administrationId.title: Administration ID
administrationId.description: Which administration this declaration belongs to.
administrationId.x-notes: The administration this declaration belongs to (wkr-administration REQ-WKR-001). Plain string, not a $ref (ADR-062 rule 7, the PayrollRun convention -- no Administration schema is modeled in humaniq).

year.title: Year
year.description: The tax year this counts towards — the work-related costs budget is a whole-year budget.
year.x-notes: Fiscal year this declaration counts toward -- the vrije ruimte is a whole-year budget (wkr-administration REQ-WKR-001).

date.title: Date
date.description: Date the allowance/benefit was granted, invoiced, or made available.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the allowance was for, for example 'Personeelsuitje juni'.
description.x-notes: Free-text description of the vergoeding/verstrekking (e.g. "Personeelsuitje juni").

wkrCategory.title: WKR category
wkrCategory.description: How this allowance is treated: charged to the free margin, specifically exempt, or already taxed as a final levy.
wkrCategory.x-notes: WKR classification (wkr-administration REQ-WKR-001, design.md D1): `vrije-ruimte` consumes the administration's vrije ruimte; `gericht-vrijgesteld` is a statutory gerichte vrijstelling that stays outside it (nl-wkr-gerichte-vrijstelling, judgemental, unchanged by this schema); `eindheffing` is loon the employer already designated as eindheffingsloon. Only `vrije-ruimte` amounts are summed into vrijeRuimteUsed.

employeeId.title: Employee ID
employeeId.description: The employee this concerns. Leave empty for a company-wide allowance.
employeeId.x-notes: The employee this declaration concerns, or null for a collective/company-wide allowance (wkr-administration REQ-WKR-001).

sourceReference.title: Source reference
sourceReference.description: Invoice/journal reference for the audit trail (e.g. "INV-2026-0612").

WntDisclosure.title: WNT disclosure
WntDisclosure.description: The annual WNT-verantwoording for one topfunctionaris for one calendar year (Wet normering topinkomens, BWBR0032249). One row per (topfunctionaris, year) carrying the hand-entered total WNT-bezoldiging for that year and a two-state concept -> gepubliceerd publication lifecycle. The set of a year's WntDisclosure rows IS that year's WNT-verantwoording -- there is no separate aggregate report schema (wnt-disclosure design.md D2). totalCompensation is hand-entered by finance; this app computes and aggregates nothing (design.md D3).

publiceren.description: Publishes the disclosure as part of the year's WNT-verantwoording. No guard -- publication is a plain per-row status transition (wnt-disclosure design.md D2).

year.title: Year
year.description: The calendar year this disclosure covers.
year.x-notes: The calendar year this disclosure covers, in YYYY. The year's full WNT-verantwoording is every WntDisclosure row carrying this year (design.md D2).

totalCompensation.title: Total compensation
totalCompensation.description: Total remuneration for the year in whole euros: salary, holiday allowance, year-end bonus, taxable expense reimbursements and pension contribution.
totalCompensation.x-notes: The total WNT-bezoldiging for this topfunctionaris for the year, in whole euro (salary + vacation allowance + year-end bonus + taxable expense reimbursements + pension contribution, per the WNT's own compensation definition). Hand-entered by finance -- this app computes and aggregates nothing across payroll runs (design.md D3). Compared against the WNT-norm's annual figure (EUR 262.000 in 2026) by nl-wnt-norm-overschrijding.
